about: The slots of a screen brief (specification 0010): every choice a builder of one screen meets, as a closed list. `reads` says where the answer of a slot is read from; a slot with nothing to read from says so with `unheld`, whose `when` is `always`, or `planned` for a slot a ledger holds only once the screen is built. A slot is never dropped from a sheet: one with no answer is open and says why. `ask` is what an open slot puts to the owner: `recommend`, what a builder goes on with until the owner answers, `basis`, what that rests on (a `principle`, a `standard` or a `measurement`; the sheet adds what it read of the repository), and `hard_to_undo`. `cases` holds another `recommend` for a case the sheet reads or measures, by the case's name, with {name} where the sheet puts what it measured; the slot's own `recommend` stands where no case is named. The slots are the choices every screen meets and not every question of one screen: the sheet says so, and names where other choices hide. A recommendation never makes up an answer the sheet has no source for: where only the owner has it, it says where the answer is written before the screen is built. Adding or removing a slot is the owner's call.

states.settled: the repository answers it, and the sheet names the file and the row or line the answer comes from
states.asked: a question about this slot of this screen waits on the owner
states.open: nothing in the repository says, and the sheet says so

slots.name: kind and reference screen
slots.question: Of which kind is the screen, and which screen is it built like?
reads: the `family` of the screen's row in the ledger of screens
the page of that kind, and the reference screen the page names

ask.recommend: Do not build the screen until its row names a kind that has a page with a reference screen: give the row such a kind, or ask for the new kind on its own.

basis.text: The floor's rule that every screen is of one kind, and that a kind has a page naming the screen to build it like.

slots.name: what the screen shows
slots.question: Which records does the screen show, with which fields?
reads: the `shows` of the screen's row
the fields of each entity in the data model, and the column type each field names

ask.recommend: Write into the screen's row what it shows, as entities of the data model, before it is built: the sheet has no source to recommend a record from.

basis.text: The floor's rule that a screen's row says what the screen shows, and that the gate reads it from there.

slots.name: actions and roles
slots.question: Which action opens the screen, which actions does it offer, and who may run each?
reads: the `entry` and the `actions` of the screen's row
the roles that hold each action in the data model
the rules page's line on the mark a control of an action carries

ask.recommend: Write into the screen's row the action that opens it and the actions it has buttons for, each given only to roles the data model lists, before it is built.

basis.text: The floor's rule that a screen's row names its entry and its actions, and that who may run each is read from the data model.

slots.name: states
slots.question: Which states must the screen have, and where is the way into each written?
reads: the `states` of the screen's row
the state table
the screen list of the application, which says how each state is reached

ask.recommend: Give the screen every state the state table requires, and list them in its row.

basis.text: The state table of the repository, which every screen follows unless it is excused there with a reason.

slots.name: components
slots.question: Which components is the screen built from, and what may it not use?
reads: the component ledger
the frame the page of the kind names, and what that page forbids outside the frame

ask.recommend: Build the screen only from components the component ledger lists, inside the frame the page of its kind names: where either is missing, write it there before the screen is built.

basis.text: The floor's rule that a screen is built from the repository's own components, in the frame of its kind.

slots.name: words
slots.question: Where do the words of the screen come from, and which terms does it use?
reads: the rows of the decisions ledger in the content layer
the `title` of the screen's row

ask.recommend: Keep every word the screen shows in the one place the repository keeps its words, and give the decisions ledger a row of the content layer that says where that is.

basis.text: The floor's rule that a screen writes no word itself.

slots.name: rules that apply
slots.question: Which rules does the screen follow?
reads: the lines of the rules page that apply to the screen, one rule a line

ask.recommend: Write the rules page with the plugin's own guide, with paths that take in the screen's file, before the screen is built.

basis.text: The floor's rule that the rules page is what a builder reads before it touches a screen: what the gate holds is told there.

slots.name: principles and direction
slots.question: What did the owner fix before any value?
reads: the principles the owner fixed and the direction they took, in the blueprint, through the reader the rules page and the review share

ask.recommend: Build with no principle to rest on, and ask each choice the ledgers leave open: fixing a principle or taking a direction is the owner's, with the guide.

basis.text: The floor's rule that only a principle the owner fixed, or a direction they took, settles a choice: one that stands in the blueprint unconfirmed settles nothing.

slots.name: widths and checks
slots.question: At which widths is the screen checked, and what will grade it?
reads: the widths the repository declares
the checks the rows of the decisions ledger name

ask.recommend: Check the screen at the two widths every floor starts from, and grade it with the repository's own gate, until the repository declares its widths and its checks.

basis.text: WCAG 2.2, reflow: a page works at a width of 320 CSS pixels; the wide one is the width a floor starts from.

slots.name: changes to the data model
slots.question: Does the screen need an action or an entity the data model does not have?
reads: computed: each action and entity the screen's row names, looked up in the data model

ask.recommend: Add each action and entity the row names and the data model lacks to the data model first, in the same change, and say in the change's description that the data model changed, so that a person reviews it before it merges.

written.recommend: Keep what this branch wrote into the data model as it is written until the owner answers, and say in the change's description that the data model changed, with each name and its shape, so that a person reviews it before it merges. Where another shape was possible (a field of its own, or one more value of a field that is there), say which was taken and why.

basis.text: The floor's rule that a screen never names a concept or an action the data model does not have.

slots.name: place in the navigation
slots.question: Where does the screen stand among the screens of the application?
reads: the screen list of the application, for a screen that is built

unheld.why: no ledger holds where a screen that is not built yet goes in the navigation

ask.recommend: Give the screen the last place among the screens of the application, reached through the application's frame alone, so that no screen that is there moves.

basis.text: The order of the screens of the application as it stands: a screen added last moves none of them.

slots.name: other screens it touches
slots.question: Does another screen change because of this one?

unheld.why: no ledger holds which other screens a screen changes

ask.recommend: Change no other screen: build this one alone, and where another screen must change, that is a change of that screen, with a sheet of its own.

look.recommend: Do not take it that no other screen changes. Before this screen is built, look at {screens}, for what the sheet read of each: change in the same change each one that must change for this screen to work, after a sheet of its own (run the brief of that screen first), leave the others as they are, and say in the change's description which screens changed and why.

basis.text: What the rows of the other screens of the ledger name, and what the data model says of the actions on the records this screen shows: a screen that shares nothing with this one has no reason to change, and one that shares a record or an action is looked at before it is left alone.
